claims.title: Binary latent-mixture emission TV equals latent-weight TV times emission-row separation
claims.scope: two latent components with known categorical emission rows and arbitrary binary mixing weights
assumptions: both mixing hypotheses use the same two emission rows
nonclaims: the scalar identity is specific to a two-component mixture
with unknown emission rows the mixing weight is not identifiable from one emission per unit (label switching and non-unique representations)

claims.title: Identical binary latent emission rows make the mixing weight observationally unidentifiable
assumptions: only the declared emissions are observed
nonclaims: additional interventions or observations could change identifiability

claims.title: Observed-law TV uncertainty transfers to binary latent-weight uncertainty with inverse row-separation amplification
claims.scope: binary mixtures with positive emission-row TV separation d
assumptions: the compared latent and observed laws remain in the declared mixture family
nonclaims: the amplified radius may be conservative when additional structure is available
for an off-family observed centre Q_hat with TV(Q_hat,Q_theta)<=rho, only the set {theta': TV(Q_hat,Q_theta')<=rho}, of diameter at most 2rho/d, is controlled

claims.title: Binary Bernoulli emission calibration inflates latent-weight squared uncertainty by inverse row separation squared
claims.scope: N independent units with one Bernoulli emission each from a binary latent mixture with known row probabilities
assumptions: emissions are conditionally independent across units given their latent draws (one emission per unit)
theta_hat is clipped to [0,1] when the sample frequency falls off the mixture segment
nonclaims: the fixed-sample Markov bound is not claimed optimal

claims.title: Halving binary emission-row separation quadruples the fixed-sample latent squared-radius inflation
claims.scope: clean Bernoulli rows 0 versus 1 compared with noisy rows 1/4 versus 3/4 at equal N and alpha
assumptions: equal N and alpha in both designs
nonclaims: the factor four is a property of the conservative worst-case-variance (1/(4N)) bound; the exact sampling-variance ratio depends on theta and is not claimed to equal four

claims.title: Bounded exact binary latent-mixture identifiability audit
claims.scope: multicategory TV identity, identical-row nonidentifiability, radius amplification, Bernoulli inversion, and inverse-square sample conditioning tests
assumptions: all probabilities and radii use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded checks are not evidence for simulation
CI success is not empirical validation of latent-mixture assumptions
